name: niri
summary: Scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor: windows sit in columns on an infinite horizontal strip, and opening a window never resizes the others. KDL config with live reload, focus ring, borders, per-window corner radius, tabbed columns and named workspaces.

install.notes: Fedora 43 updates and 44 carry 26.04. The Copr yalter/niri (releases) and yalter/niri-git (nightly) are maintained by the author: dnf copr enable yalter/niri.

linux.notes: Latest release at verification: v26.04. Config loads from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/niri/config.kdl, falling back to /etc/niri/config.kdl; if neither exists niri writes the default there. No official Debian or Ubuntu package is documented in the wiki (a community pacstall package exists); build from source or use a distro that ships it. Wayland only: X11 apps need xwayland-satellite (niri starts it when installed). The binds {} section is not filled with defaults when omitted, so keep the default binds when editing. Niri has no layout types to pick: windows are always columns, so a left-plus-two-stacked-right terminal layout is built by moving windows into columns.
